title: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) staging and mutual exclusivity (Stages 1–5)
text: KDIGO guidelines classify chronic kidney disease into mutually exclusive stages by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR): Stage 1 (eGFR >= 90 mL/min/1.73m2 with kidney damage), Stage 2 (eGFR 60–89), Stage 3 (eGFR 30–59), Stage 4 (eGFR 15–29), and Stage 5 (< 15 or dialysis). A patient can only be in one current CKD stage at a time; when CKD progresses (for example, from Stage 1 to Stage 2 and then Stage 3), earlier stages should be marked resolved rather than left simultaneously active on the problem list.
source: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease / NIDDK
license: US Public Domain (NIDDK) / KDIGO Clinical Summary

title: Prediabetes vs. Type 2 Diabetes and Diabetic Kidney Disease progression
text: Prediabetes (HbA1c 5.7%–6.4%, SNOMED 714628002) is a precursor state before overt Type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c >= 6.5%). Once a patient develops established Type 2 diabetes complications—such as diabetic kidney disease (SNOMED 127013003), diabetic microalbuminuria (SNOMED 90781000119102), or diabetic proteinuria (SNOMED 157141000119108) requiring glucose-lowering therapy—the earlier Prediabetes entry is clinically superseded and should be reconciled as resolved.
source: American Diabetes Association (ADA) Standards of Care in Diabetes / MedlinePlus

title: CDC ACIP HPV immunization schedule: 2-dose (under age 15) vs. 3-dose rule
text: CDC ACIP recommends a 2-dose HPV vaccination schedule (0 and 6–12 months; minimum interval 5 months) for immunocompetent adolescents who initiate the vaccine series before their 15th birthday (ages 9–14 years). A 3-dose schedule (0, 1–2, and 6 months) is required when the series is started at age 15 years or older, for immunocompromised individuals, or when the first two doses in a younger starter are administered less than 5 months apart. Administering a 3rd HPV dose (CVX 62 or 165) to an immunocompetent adolescent who received Dose 1 before age 15 and Dose 2 at least 5 months later is an ACIP over-immunization schedule anomaly.
source: CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) HPV Vaccine Recommendations

title: CDC ACIP Zoster (Shingles) vaccine: single-dose live Zostavax vs. 2-dose Shingrix
text: Live attenuated zoster vaccine (Zostavax, CVX 121) was a single-dose shingles vaccine that was discontinued in the United States in November 2020. Current CDC ACIP guidelines recommend 2 doses of recombinant adjuvanted zoster vaccine (Shingrix, CVX 187) spaced 2 to 6 months apart for adults aged 50 and older. Two recorded doses of live zoster vaccine (CVX 121) represent an immunization schedule or coding anomaly.
source: CDC ACIP Shingles (Herpes Zoster) Vaccination Guidelines

title: Cross-source immunization deduplication across EHRs and State Registries (WA IIS)
text: When aggregating health records from multiple sources (such as a primary care EHR, retail pharmacy, and a state immunization information system such as WA IIS), a single vaccination event is frequently reported twice with dates differing by 1 to 2 days due to administration date vs. registry transmission/claim date. Seasonal Influenza (CVX 140) or COVID-19 mRNA (CVX 208) doses recorded within 14 days of each other across different organizations should be flagged as likely duplicate immunization records rather than separate doses.
source: CDC AIRA / HL7 FHIR Immunization Implementation Guide — Deduplication Best Practices

title: Medication reconciliation: Clopidogrel vs. Plavix brand-generic equivalence
text: Clopidogrel (RxNorm 309362) and Plavix (RxNorm 213169) are the generic and brand names for the same P2Y12 antiplatelet ingredient. Concurrent active prescriptions for generic clopidogrel and brand Plavix across care settings represent brand-generic therapeutic duplication that increases bleeding risk.
source: DailyMed / NLM RxNorm Medication Reconciliation Guidance — Clopidogrel Bisulfate

title: Medication reconciliation: Concurrent statin class duplication (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors)
text: Simvastatin (RxNorm 312961) and Atorvastatin (Lipitor, RxNorm 617311) both belong to the HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin) therapeutic class. Concurrent active orders for two different statins constitute same-class duplication and increase the risk of myopathy, rhabdomyolysis, and transaminase elevation unless reconciled to a single intended regimen.
source: ACC/AHA Blood Cholesterol Guideline / MedlinePlus Drug Information

title: Medication reconciliation: Lisinopril vs. Prinivil brand-generic ACE inhibitor equivalence
text: Lisinopril (RxNorm 314076) and Prinivil (RxNorm 206765, also marketed as Zestril) contain the same active angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor ingredient. Concurrent active orders for generic lisinopril and brand Prinivil across different clinics represent brand-generic duplication that increases the risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and acute kidney injury.

title: Data Segmentation for Privacy (DS4P) handling of sensitive SDOH problem-list entries
text: Electronic health records may store social determinants of health (SDOH) and personal safety findings—such as criminal history (SNOMED 266948004), intimate partner abuse (SNOMED 706893006), or social isolation (SNOMED 423315002 / 55600006)—on the FHIR Condition problem list alongside medical diagnoses. Under HL7 FHIR DS4P guidance, sensitive SDOH categories are segmented from `external_share` summaries unless explicitly authorized.
source: ONC Cures Act / HIPAA Privacy Rule & HL7 FHIR DS4P (Data Segmentation for Privacy)

title: Standard reference ranges for kidney function (eGFR, Creatinine) and HbA1c
text: Core renal and glycemic reference ranges: (1) Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR, LOINC 33914-3): >= 90 mL/min/1.73m2 normal, 60–89 mildly reduced, 30–59 moderate reduction (Stage 3), 15–29 severe reduction (Stage 4), < 15 kidney failure; (2) Serum Creatinine (LOINC 2160-0 / 38483-4): typical adult reference ~0.6–1.3 mg/dL depending on sex and muscle mass; (3) Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c, LOINC 4548-4): < 5.7% normal, 5.7%–6.4% prediabetes range, >= 6.5% diabetes diagnostic threshold.
source: MedlinePlus Lab Tests / National Kidney Foundation Consumer Reference
